title: Fisher & Paykel Healthcare Airvo 3 High-Flow Oxygen System - Airway Pressure Is High, Low, or Inaccurate
description: Troubleshoots abnormal pressure-related indications or clinical observations caused by interfaces, tubing, obstruction, setup, flow settings, or measurement conditions.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Maintain Therapy
steps.instructions: If excessive, insufficient, or questionable pressure is suspected during therapy, place the patient on appropriate verified respiratory support before technical troubleshooting. Expected outcome: Patient support does not depend on equipment with questionable performance.

steps.title: 2. Clarify What Is Being Reported as Pressure
steps.instructions: Determine whether the complaint comes from an Airvo 3 alarm or indication, an external measurement, another clinical monitor, or staff observation. Record the complete message and current setup. High-flow systems should not be evaluated as though they are conventional pressure-controlled ventilators. Expected outcome: The source of the pressure concern is clearly identified.

steps.title: 3. Inspect the Patient Interface
steps.instructions: Verify that the approved interface is correctly fitted and is not blocked, occluded, damaged, folded, or otherwise improperly positioned. Expected outcome: The patient interface presents no obvious abnormal restriction or connection problem.

steps.title: 4. Inspect the Breathing Tube
steps.instructions: Check for kinks, compression, obstruction, accumulated condensate, damaged tubing, or incorrect routing. Expected outcome: The tubing path is open and correctly routed. If correcting an obstruction resolves the abnormal condition, proceed to final verification.

steps.title: 5. Inspect the Chamber and Accessible Gas Path
steps.instructions: Verify proper humidifier chamber installation and that accessible gas-path connections are secure and unobstructed. Expected outcome: No external restriction or leak is found in the gas path.

steps.title: 6. Verify Flow and Configuration
steps.instructions: Confirm that the device's displayed settings correspond with the intended clinical configuration. An unexpectedly high or low flow setting can affect pressure within an open high-flow interface. Do not modify prescribed settings on a patient solely for troubleshooting. Expected outcome: Configuration is appropriate and does not explain the reported pressure condition.

steps.title: 7. Verify External Measurement Setup
steps.instructions: If pressure was measured using separate test equipment, inspect the test setup, adapters, tubing, zeroing, and connections. Use appropriate approved equipment and applicable procedures. Expected outcome: The reported pressure condition is not caused by an incorrect external measurement setup.

steps.title: 8. Compare With Known-Good Accessories
steps.instructions: If an interface, breathing tube, chamber, or adapter remains suspect, replace it with a known-good approved compatible component and repeat the controlled test. Expected outcome: The abnormal result disappears if an external accessory was responsible.

steps.title: 9. Perform Controlled Functional Verification
steps.instructions: Verify airflow, alarms, controls, humidification, and any applicable pressure-related performance using manufacturer-defined service procedures. Do not create pressure specifications or tolerances that are not documented. Expected outcome: The system operates within applicable criteria. If so, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 10. Escalate Persistent Abnormal Pressure Behavior
steps.instructions: If external restrictions, interfaces, settings, and measurement methods are verified but the abnormal pressure condition remains, stop troubleshooting at the external level. Expected outcome: The unit is removed from service for qualified technical evaluation.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported unusually high pressure behavior while setting up the Airvo 3.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the patient-interface tubing was partially occluded by incorrect positioning.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering corrected the tubing position, verified unobstructed flow and normal operation, and completed functional testing before return to service.

title: Fisher & Paykel Healthcare Airvo 3 High-Flow Oxygen System - Battery Will Not Charge or Runtime Is Short
description: Troubleshoots charging, AC-power, battery-status, environmental, and operating conditions associated with inadequate battery charging or unexpectedly short runtime.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Maintain Therapy
steps.instructions: Do not test questionable battery operation while a patient depends on the Airvo 3. If reliable operation cannot be assured, place the patient on an appropriate verified alternative device or maintain the Airvo 3 on reliable AC power as clinically appropriate. Expected outcome: Patient therapy is not dependent on an unverified battery.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Battery Complaint
steps.instructions: Determine whether the battery does not indicate charging, never reaches an expected state of charge, discharges unusually quickly, or causes the device to shut down when AC power is removed. Record displayed battery indicators or messages and determine the conditions under which the problem occurs. Expected outcome: The charging or runtime problem is clearly defined.

steps.title: 3. Verify Reliable AC Power
steps.instructions: Confirm the Airvo 3 is connected to an approved functioning receptacle and that the external power connection is secure. Test the outlet using approved methods or compare operation at a known-good outlet. Expected outcome: Reliable AC power is available to the device. If charging begins normally after correcting the outlet or connection, the cause has been identified.

steps.title: 4. Inspect the Power Cord and Accessible Connections
steps.instructions: Inspect the power cord, plug, and accessible connection points for looseness, physical damage, contamination, or overheating. Replace damaged external power components only with approved compatible components. Expected outcome: The charging path is not being interrupted by an obvious external power connection problem.

steps.title: 5. Review Battery and Charging Indications
steps.instructions: With the device connected to AC power, observe the normal battery and charging indications. Note warnings, unusual status changes, or failure to recognize the battery. Do not access internal battery connections or bypass battery monitoring. Expected outcome: The device recognizes the battery and indicates normal charging behavior. Persistent abnormal indication requires further evaluation.

steps.title: 6. Allow an Appropriate Charging Opportunity
steps.instructions: If the battery was deeply discharged or the device had been stored, allow it to remain connected to reliable AC power under normal approved conditions before evaluating runtime. Do not declare the battery defective solely because it was initially at a low state of charge. Expected outcome: Battery charge indication increases appropriately. If charging remains absent or abnormal, proceed to escalation.

steps.title: 7. Consider Operating Conditions
steps.instructions: Determine whether short runtime was observed under unusual operating conditions, after extended storage, repeated battery operation, or in an inappropriate environmental condition. Confirm ventilation openings are unobstructed and the device is being operated within its intended environment. Expected outcome: No external operating condition explains the reduced runtime, or correcting the condition restores acceptable operation.

steps.title: 8. Compare Battery Performance Under Controlled Conditions
steps.instructions: If permitted by facility procedure and manufacturer guidance, operate the device off AC power in a controlled nonclinical setting and observe battery behavior. Do not rely on an improvised runtime threshold. Use manufacturer documentation or approved service criteria when determining whether runtime is acceptable. Expected outcome: Battery operation is stable and consistent with applicable service criteria. If not, remove the unit from service for battery-system evaluation.

steps.title: 9. Complete Final Functional Verification
steps.instructions: After correcting an AC connection or charging problem, verify reliable AC operation, charging indication, transition to battery operation if applicable, alarms, airflow, and normal device function. Expected outcome: Charging and battery operation are reliable. Troubleshooting can stop when required return-to-service testing passes.

steps.title: 10. Escalate Persistent Battery Problems
steps.instructions: If external AC power and connections are correct but the battery is not recognized, will not charge, or cannot meet approved runtime expectations, stop external troubleshooting. Expected outcome: The Airvo 3 is removed from service for qualified battery or charging-system evaluation.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported the Airvo 3 battery was not charging while the unit was connected to AC power.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the power cord connection at the device was loose, preventing consistent AC operation and charging.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering secured the connection, verified normal charging indication and battery operation, and completed functional testing before return to service.

helpfulDetails: Battery indication at time of complaint

title: Fisher & Paykel Healthcare Airvo 3 High-Flow Oxygen System - Delivered Flow or Volume Is Low or Unstable
description: Troubleshoots low or unstable delivered flow associated with setup, tubing, interface, obstruction, settings, gas supply, or environmental conditions.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Maintain Therapy
steps.instructions: Treat inadequate or unstable flow as a therapy reliability issue. Move the patient to appropriate verified respiratory support before performing troubleshooting that could interrupt flow. Expected outcome: Required therapy continues safely while the Airvo 3 is evaluated.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Reported Flow Problem
steps.instructions: Determine whether low flow is indicated by the device, measured during technical testing, perceived by staff, or associated with alarms or unstable operation. Record the configured flow setting and any displayed message. Expected outcome: The reported condition is clearly characterized.

steps.title: 3. Check the Patient Interface
steps.instructions: Inspect the nasal interface or other approved patient interface for incorrect sizing, disconnection, damage, obstruction, or poor positioning. Expected outcome: The interface is intact, correctly connected, and appropriately positioned. Correcting an external interface problem restores expected delivery.

steps.title: 4. Inspect the Heated Breathing Tube
steps.instructions: Check the full accessible tubing path for kinks, crushing, excessive bending, disconnection, water accumulation, damage, or obstruction. Expected outcome: The breathing tube is open, intact, and securely connected.

steps.title: 5. Inspect the Humidifier Chamber and Gas Path
steps.instructions: Verify correct chamber installation and inspect accessible gas-path connections for poor seating, damage, or obstruction. Expected outcome: External gas-path components are assembled correctly and do not restrict airflow.

steps.title: 6. Verify the Configured Flow Setting
steps.instructions: Confirm that the displayed flow setting matches the intended clinical setup. Do not change prescribed therapy settings solely for troubleshooting unless authorized and performed in a nonclinical test condition. Expected outcome: The device configuration matches the intended setting and the symptom is not caused by an incorrect control setting.

steps.title: 7. Check Oxygen and External Gas Connections When Used
steps.instructions: If supplemental oxygen is connected, inspect the external oxygen tubing, connectors, supply source, and routing. Confirm that gas-supply problems are not affecting overall system operation. Expected outcome: External gas connections are secure and available as intended.

steps.title: 8. Substitute Known-Good External Components
steps.instructions: Using approved compatible components, substitute the breathing tube, chamber, interface, or relevant external accessory one component at a time when an accessory problem remains possible. Expected outcome: Flow becomes stable if an external component was responsible. Replace the identified defective component.

steps.title: 9. Verify Delivered Performance
steps.instructions: In a controlled nonpatient test setup, verify that the device produces stable flow using appropriate approved test equipment and manufacturer-defined service methods where required. Do not invent acceptable flow tolerances. Expected outcome: Delivered performance meets applicable manufacturer criteria. If verified, troubleshooting can stop after completing return-to-service testing.

steps.title: 10. Escalate Persistent Flow Instability
steps.instructions: If settings, circuit components, gas supply, connections, and external restrictions are correct but delivered flow remains low or unstable, stop external troubleshooting. Expected outcome: The Airvo 3 is removed from service for qualified evaluation of its flow-generation and sensing systems.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that airflow from the Airvo 3 was intermittently low during setup.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the heated breathing tube was sharply kinked behind the equipment stand.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering corrected the tubing routing, verified stable airflow and normal alarms, and completed functional verification before return to service.

title: Fisher & Paykel Healthcare Airvo 3 High-Flow Oxygen System - Device Will Not Power On or Complete Self-Test
description: Troubleshoots startup, power, connection, accessory, and environmental conditions that can prevent the Airvo 3 from powering on or becoming ready.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Maintain Therapy
steps.instructions: If the Airvo 3 is supporting a patient and becomes unavailable or unreliable, transfer the patient to an appropriate verified alternative source of respiratory support before troubleshooting. Do not troubleshoot a questionable high-flow oxygen system while a patient depends on it. Expected outcome: Patient therapy remains safely supported independent of the affected device.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Reported Condition
steps.instructions: Determine whether the unit is completely unresponsive, begins startup and shuts down, displays a message, produces an alarm, or consistently stops during self-test. Ask whether the problem occurs on AC power, battery operation, or both. Document any displayed message before cycling power. Expected outcome: The failure is clearly defined and reproducible. If the unit subsequently starts normally and completes its startup checks, continue with final functional verification before returning it to service.

steps.title: 3. Inspect for Obvious Damage or Unsafe Conditions
steps.instructions: Inspect the enclosure, power cord, plug, connectors, humidifier area, and accessible accessories for damage, contamination, liquid intrusion, overheating, unusual odor, or evidence of impact. Do not energize equipment with evidence of liquid intrusion, electrical damage, or overheating. Expected outcome: No condition is found that requires immediate removal from service. If damage or contamination makes operation unsafe, stop troubleshooting and remove the device from service.

steps.title: 4. Verify the AC Power Source
steps.instructions: Confirm the power cord is fully connected to the Airvo 3 and an appropriate AC receptacle. Test the receptacle using approved methods or connect the device to another known-good approved outlet. Avoid assuming an internal power failure until facility power and cord connections have been verified. Expected outcome: The device receives reliable AC power. If it starts and completes self-test normally after correcting the outlet or connection, the issue is resolved and troubleshooting can stop after final verification.

steps.title: 5. Inspect the External Power Cord and Connections
steps.instructions: Inspect the accessible power cord and plug for cuts, bent contacts, looseness, discoloration, or other damage. If permitted by facility policy, compare operation with a known-good compatible power cord where applicable. Expected outcome: External power components are secure and undamaged. A defective external power component is replaced with an approved compatible item and normal startup is restored.

steps.title: 6. Remove Nonessential External Accessories
steps.instructions: Disconnect nonessential external data or communication accessories that can safely be removed without altering required device configuration. Leave required respiratory components installed as specified for normal operation. Restart the unit using the normal operating controls. Expected outcome: The Airvo 3 completes startup with its normal required configuration. If an external accessory is identified as the cause, replace or correct that accessory and verify operation.

steps.title: 7. Allow the Device to Complete Its Normal Startup Sequence
steps.instructions: Observe the complete startup process without repeatedly interrupting it. Note where startup stops and record any message or alarm exactly as displayed. Do not bypass self-tests or enter unauthorized service functions. Expected outcome: Startup completes and the device reaches its normal ready state. If it repeatedly fails at the same point, proceed to escalation.

steps.title: 8. Perform Final Functional Verification
steps.instructions: After correcting an external problem, configure the Airvo 3 with appropriate approved accessories and verify normal startup, display operation, alarm indication, airflow generation, and humidification readiness using facility procedures and applicable manufacturer documentation. Expected outcome: The device consistently completes startup and performs normally. Troubleshooting can stop and the unit may be returned to service when required return-to-service checks pass.

steps.title: 9. Escalate an Unresolved Startup Failure
steps.instructions: If known-good AC power, accessible connections, external accessories, and normal restart procedures have been verified but the Airvo 3 remains unresponsive or cannot complete self-test, do not proceed into unauthorized internal repair. Expected outcome: The device is removed from service and referred for qualified bench evaluation or manufacturer-authorized service.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported the Airvo 3 would not power on when connected for patient use.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the AC power connection was not fully seated and verified the outlet and power cord were otherwise functional.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering secured the power connection, confirmed normal startup and self-test completion, and completed functional verification before returning the device to service.

helpfulDetails: Whether the device was completely unresponsive or stopped during startup
Evidence of liquid, impact, heat, or odor

title: Fisher & Paykel Healthcare Airvo 3 High-Flow Oxygen System - Display, Controls, or Alarm Audio Fails
description: Troubleshoots display, control-response, indicator, alarm-audio, power, obstruction, accessory, and software symptoms affecting safe operation.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Maintain Therapy
steps.instructions: A high-flow oxygen system with an unreliable display, control interface, or audible alarm should not remain in clinical use. Transfer the patient to appropriate verified respiratory support before troubleshooting. Expected outcome: Patient therapy and alarm coverage are maintained independently of the affected device.

steps.title: 2. Confirm Which Function Has Failed
steps.instructions: Determine whether the screen is blank, frozen, unreadable, intermittently responsive, or whether controls fail to respond. For alarm complaints, determine whether visual indication occurs without audible output or whether the entire alarm function appears abnormal. Expected outcome: The affected user-interface or alarm function is clearly identified.

steps.title: 3. Verify Stable Power
steps.instructions: Confirm the device has reliable AC power and inspect battery status where applicable. A marginal power connection can cause intermittent display or control behavior. Expected outcome: The complaint is not caused by loss or instability of external power.

steps.title: 4. Inspect the Display and Controls Externally
steps.instructions: Check for physical damage, contamination, cracked surfaces, liquid exposure, labels or protective materials obstructing controls, or anything pressing continuously against the user interface. Do not disassemble the display or control panel. Expected outcome: No external physical condition interferes with normal operation.

steps.title: 5. Clean External Control Surfaces if Appropriate
steps.instructions: If contamination is present, clean the exterior according to approved device cleaning procedures and allow it to dry as required before retesting. Expected outcome: Controls respond normally if contamination was preventing proper operation.

steps.title: 6. Perform a Normal Restart
steps.instructions: With the device removed from patient use, shut it down and restart it using normal operating controls. Observe startup, display behavior, indicators, and alarm audio. Do not use undocumented reset procedures. Expected outcome: The display and controls initialize normally and remain responsive.

steps.title: 7. Check Relevant Settings
steps.instructions: Verify that user-accessible display and audio settings have not been unintentionally changed where such controls are available. Do not disable required alarms or modify restricted configuration settings. Expected outcome: A user-accessible setting is not causing the reported symptom.

steps.title: 8. Verify Alarm Operation
steps.instructions: Using an approved functional test method, verify that applicable alarm conditions produce the expected visual and audible notification. Do not deliberately create unsafe clinical conditions to test alarms. Expected outcome: Audible and visual alarm functions operate reliably. If alarm audio remains absent or intermittent, remove the device from service.

steps.title: 9. Observe for Intermittent Failure
steps.instructions: Allow the system to operate under a controlled test condition while checking display response and controls. Do not return an intermittently freezing or unresponsive interface to clinical use simply because it restarted once. Expected outcome: Controls, display, and alarms remain consistently functional.

steps.title: 10. Complete Final Functional Verification
steps.instructions: Verify startup, airflow, controls, display, audible and visual alarms, humidification, and overall operation. Expected outcome: All critical user-interface and alarm functions work reliably. Troubleshooting can stop and the unit may be returned to service.

steps.title: 11. Escalate Persistent Interface or Alarm Failure
steps.instructions: If stable power, external condition, restart, and settings have been checked but the display, controls, or alarm audio remain unreliable, stop external troubleshooting. Expected outcome: The Airvo 3 is removed from service for qualified technical evaluation.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that the Airvo 3 screen was operating but alarm audio could not be heard during setup.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering confirmed the audible alarm function remained absent after verifying power, settings, and normal restart.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering removed the device from service, labeled it Out of Service, and sent it for qualified repair and complete alarm verification before return to use.

helpfulDetails: Blank, frozen, or intermittent display behavior
Evidence of contamination or liquid exposure

title: Fisher & Paykel Healthcare Airvo 3 High-Flow Oxygen System - Flow Sensor or Exhalation Valve Is Not Recognized
description: Troubleshoots sensor or gas-path recognition complaints by verifying the actual Airvo 3 configuration, compatible accessories, connections, and displayed fault information.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Maintain Therapy
steps.instructions: If the Airvo 3 cannot reliably recognize a required component or establish normal airflow, transfer the patient to an appropriate verified respiratory support system before troubleshooting. Expected outcome: Patient support remains uninterrupted.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Reported Message
steps.instructions: Record the exact device message or alarm rather than relying only on the description "flow sensor" or "exhalation valve." The Airvo 3 is a high-flow oxygen system and should not be assumed to use the same external flow-sensor or exhalation-valve arrangement as a conventional ventilator. Verify which component the device is actually identifying. Expected outcome: The complaint is tied to an actual installed component, connector, or displayed message.

steps.title: 3. Verify the Intended Patient-Circuit Configuration
steps.instructions: Compare the installed breathing tube, humidifier chamber, patient interface, and adapters with the intended approved Airvo 3 setup. Do not add, bypass, or substitute a ventilator-style exhalation valve unless it is specifically part of the approved configuration being serviced. Expected outcome: The respiratory system is assembled with the correct compatible components.

steps.title: 4. Inspect External Connections
steps.instructions: Inspect accessible breathing-tube and accessory connections for incomplete insertion, contamination, moisture, damage, bent contacts where applicable, or poor seating. Expected outcome: All externally accessible connections are clean, intact, and fully seated.

steps.title: 5. Inspect the Breathing Tube and Accessories
steps.instructions: Check the heated breathing tube and other applicable accessories for physical damage, incorrect type, contamination, or signs that could prevent proper detection or operation. Expected outcome: Installed accessories are appropriate and undamaged.

steps.title: 6. Reseat the Applicable Accessories
steps.instructions: With the device safely removed from patient use, disconnect and reinstall the affected external component according to its normal connection method. Do not force connectors or bypass recognition features. Expected outcome: The component is recognized after correct reconnection. If so, continue to final functional verification.

steps.title: 7. Substitute a Known-Good Compatible Accessory
steps.instructions: When an external accessory is identified by the device or suspected from inspection, substitute a known-good approved compatible accessory. Expected outcome: Normal recognition with the known-good accessory identifies the original accessory as defective.

steps.title: 8. Restart and Observe Normal Initialization
steps.instructions: Restart the Airvo 3 using standard controls and observe whether the device recognizes the installed system and reaches its ready state. Expected outcome: The recognition error clears and the device completes startup normally.

steps.title: 9. Perform Final Functional Verification
steps.instructions: Verify airflow, alarms, accessory recognition, humidification, controls, and overall system performance with the complete intended configuration. Expected outcome: The Airvo 3 consistently recognizes required components and operates normally. Troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 10. Escalate Persistent Recognition Errors
steps.instructions: If the correct known-good accessories and connections have been verified but the device continues to report a component or sensing problem, stop external troubleshooting. Expected outcome: The Airvo 3 is removed from service for qualified evaluation of sensing, connector, control, or internal gas-path functions.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that the Airvo 3 would not recognize the connected breathing system during setup.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the heated breathing tube connection was not fully seated at the device.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering reconnected the tube correctly, verified normal recognition, airflow, alarms, and humidification, and returned the device to service after functional testing.

title: Fisher & Paykel Healthcare Airvo 3 High-Flow Oxygen System - Humidification or Temperature Control Fails
description: Troubleshoots inadequate heating, humidification, temperature control, chamber setup, water supply, heated-tube connections, and environmental causes.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Maintain Therapy
steps.instructions: Do not continue patient use when required humidification or temperature control is unreliable. Transfer the patient to an appropriate verified respiratory support system if troubleshooting would interrupt therapy. Expected outcome: Patient therapy remains safe while the affected system is evaluated.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Humidification or Temperature Complaint
steps.instructions: Determine whether the Airvo 3 fails to warm, produces a temperature-related alarm, has excessive or inadequate condensation, does not recognize the heated breathing system, or otherwise fails to reach its normal operating state. Record exact displayed messages and settings. Expected outcome: The specific heating or humidification failure is identified.

steps.title: 3. Inspect the Humidifier Chamber
steps.instructions: Verify that the approved chamber is correctly installed and seated. Inspect it for damage, leakage, contamination, incorrect assembly, or other obvious abnormalities. Expected outcome: The chamber is correctly installed and physically intact.

steps.title: 4. Verify Water Supply and Chamber Filling
steps.instructions: Confirm that the humidification setup has an appropriate water supply and that the chamber is filling as intended for its approved configuration. Inspect external water-supply components for kinks, clamps, poor positioning, disconnection, or empty supply. Expected outcome: Water is available to the chamber without an external supply restriction.

steps.title: 5. Inspect the Heated Breathing Tube
steps.instructions: Check the tube for damage, incorrect connection, excessive condensate, kinks, or poor routing. Inspect accessible electrical/contact areas for contamination or poor seating without probing internal contacts. Expected outcome: The heated breathing tube is correctly connected and undamaged.

steps.title: 6. Verify Compatible Accessories
steps.instructions: Confirm that the chamber, heated breathing tube, patient interface, and related accessories are approved and compatible with the Airvo 3 setup. Expected outcome: Humidification is not being compromised by an incompatible accessory.

steps.title: 7. Review Temperature Controls and Configuration
steps.instructions: Confirm that user-accessible temperature settings and configuration match the intended clinical setup. Do not alter restricted parameters or use unauthorized service menus. Expected outcome: The complaint is not caused by an incorrect accessible setting.

steps.title: 8. Check Environmental and Positioning Conditions
steps.instructions: Ensure the device and circuit are positioned as intended, ventilation openings are unobstructed, the breathing tube is not exposed to unusual cooling or heat sources, and the equipment is being used in an appropriate environment. Expected outcome: External environmental conditions are not interfering with heating or humidification.

steps.title: 9. Substitute Known-Good External Components
steps.instructions: If the chamber or heated breathing tube remains suspect, replace it with a known-good approved compatible component and repeat the test. Expected outcome: Normal heating and humidification with the replacement component identifies the original accessory as defective.

steps.title: 10. Verify Complete Humidification Operation
steps.instructions: Allow the device to operate under a controlled nonpatient test condition and verify normal warm-up, temperature indication, airflow, alarms, and humidification behavior according to applicable procedures. Expected outcome: Humidification and temperature control operate normally. Troubleshooting can stop after required return-to-service checks.

steps.title: 11. Escalate Persistent Heating Problems
steps.instructions: If water supply, chamber, tubing, accessories, settings, and environmental conditions are correct but the fault persists, stop external troubleshooting. Expected outcome: The Airvo 3 is removed from service for qualified heating, sensing, control, or power-system evaluation.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that the Airvo 3 was not humidifying properly and displayed abnormal temperature behavior.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the heated breathing tube connection was not fully seated.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering reconnected the heated breathing tube, verified normal warm-up, humidification, airflow, and alarms, and returned the unit to service after functional testing.

title: Fisher & Paykel Healthcare Airvo 3 High-Flow Oxygen System - Network, Data Export, or Software Update Fails
description: Troubleshoots supported communication, data-transfer, connection, configuration, media, and software-update problems without altering unauthorized system settings.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Separate Therapy From Connectivity
steps.instructions: Do not interrupt active respiratory therapy to troubleshoot optional communication, data export, or software functions. If troubleshooting requires restart, disconnection, or configuration changes, remove the Airvo 3 from patient use first. Expected outcome: Clinical therapy is not disrupted by technical troubleshooting.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Failure
steps.instructions: Determine whether the issue involves a supported network connection, failure to export information, failure to recognize approved media or accessories, inability to begin an update, or an update that reports an error. Record the exact message and the step at which the process fails. Expected outcome: The communication, export, or update failure is clearly defined.

steps.title: 3. Verify Normal Device Operation First
steps.instructions: Confirm that the Airvo 3 completes startup and performs its primary respiratory functions normally. A device with broader startup, power, or control problems should not be treated as an isolated connectivity problem. Expected outcome: The device itself is operational and the problem is isolated to the requested secondary function.

steps.title: 4. Inspect External Connections and Accessories
steps.instructions: Inspect applicable external communication cables, adapters, approved removable media, or network connections for damage, looseness, contamination, incorrect insertion, or incompatible components. Expected outcome: External connection hardware is intact and correctly installed.

steps.title: 5. Reseat the Applicable Connection
steps.instructions: With the device in a safe nonpatient condition, disconnect and reconnect the affected external cable, adapter, or approved media. Expected outcome: The connection is recognized and the requested operation succeeds. If so, proceed to final verification.

steps.title: 6. Substitute a Known-Good External Component
steps.instructions: When applicable, test with a known-good approved cable, adapter, media device, network port, or other external component. Change one item at a time. Expected outcome: Successful operation with the replacement identifies the original external component or infrastructure path as the cause.

steps.title: 7. Verify Network or Infrastructure Availability
steps.instructions: For supported networked functions, confirm the connected network port and required infrastructure are operational. Coordinate with IT or the responsible clinical systems team when the problem extends beyond the device. Do not alter VLANs, security settings, network addressing, or managed infrastructure without authorization. Expected outcome: The infrastructure path is confirmed available or the problem is isolated outside the Airvo 3.

steps.title: 8. Verify User-Accessible Configuration
steps.instructions: Confirm that applicable supported communication or export settings match the approved site configuration. Compare with a known-good device configuration when permitted. Do not enter restricted service menus or make undocumented configuration changes. Expected outcome: The failure is not caused by an obvious approved configuration mismatch.

steps.title: 9. Verify Software or Update Package Requirements
steps.instructions: For a software update, confirm that the update is appropriate for the exact device configuration and was obtained through an approved source. Follow manufacturer instructions exactly. Do not install unofficial software, interrupt an update unnecessarily, downgrade software without authorization, or repeatedly retry a failed update without understanding the failure. Expected outcome: The correct approved update method and package are being used.

steps.title: 10. Repeat the Function Under Controlled Conditions
steps.instructions: Retry the export, supported communication function, or approved update after external connection and infrastructure problems have been corrected. Expected outcome: The requested operation completes normally. If successful, continue to full functional verification.

steps.title: 11. Perform Final Functional Verification
steps.instructions: After any communication or software work, verify normal startup, controls, alarms, airflow, humidification, stored configuration, and any affected communication function before returning the Airvo 3 to clinical use. Expected outcome: Both primary respiratory operation and the affected secondary function are normal. Troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 12. Escalate Persistent Communication or Update Failures
steps.instructions: If known-good external connections, infrastructure, approved media, and accessible configuration have been verified but the problem remains, stop troubleshooting before making unauthorized software or internal hardware changes. Expected outcome: The device or issue is referred to the appropriate qualified service, IT, cybersecurity, or manufacturer support pathway.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that the Airvo 3 could not complete a supported data transfer.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the external communication connection was not fully seated and the device was not maintaining the data link.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering reseated the connection, verified successful data transfer, confirmed normal respiratory and alarm functions, and returned the device to service.

title: Fisher & Paykel Healthcare Airvo 3 High-Flow Oxygen System - Oxygen Concentration Is Incorrect or Will Not Calibrate
description: Troubleshoots incorrect oxygen concentration or calibration concerns involving oxygen supply, tubing, connections, settings, measurement equipment, and configuration.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Maintain Oxygen Therapy
steps.instructions: An incorrect oxygen concentration can directly affect patient care. If delivered oxygen is questionable, transfer the patient to an appropriate verified oxygen delivery system before troubleshooting. Expected outcome: Prescribed oxygen therapy is maintained independently of the affected Airvo 3.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Oxygen Complaint
steps.instructions: Determine whether the device reports an oxygen-related message, an external analyzer shows an unexpected concentration, or staff observed unstable oxygen delivery. Record the configured oxygen-related settings and the oxygen source being used. Expected outcome: The complaint is defined with objective information whenever possible.

steps.title: 3. Verify the Oxygen Source
steps.instructions: Confirm that the connected oxygen source is available, turned on where applicable, and appropriate for the intended configuration. Inspect source connections for obvious supply interruption. Expected outcome: A reliable oxygen source is available to the Airvo 3.

steps.title: 4. Inspect Oxygen Tubing and Connections
steps.instructions: Trace the external oxygen tubing from source to device. Look for disconnections, kinks, leaks, damaged tubing, loose fittings, incorrect connections, or flow restrictions. Expected outcome: The external oxygen path is secure and unobstructed. Correcting a supply connection restores stable oxygen delivery.

steps.title: 5. Verify the Device Configuration and Controls
steps.instructions: Confirm that the displayed configuration corresponds with the intended setup and oxygen source. Do not alter restricted configuration parameters or enter unauthorized service menus. Expected outcome: The observed condition is not caused by an incorrect externally accessible setting or configuration.

steps.title: 6. Verify the Oxygen Analyzer or Test Equipment
steps.instructions: If an external oxygen analyzer is being used, confirm it is appropriate for the test, in current service status, correctly connected, and functioning as expected. Compare with known-good test equipment when available. Expected outcome: The apparent oxygen error is not caused by faulty or improperly connected test equipment.

steps.title: 7. Check the Breathing Circuit
steps.instructions: Inspect the breathing tube, chamber, interfaces, and accessible gas-path components for disconnection, obstruction, or inappropriate setup that could interfere with the intended gas mixture. Expected outcome: The respiratory circuit is correctly assembled and operating normally.

steps.title: 8. Repeat Applicable Oxygen Verification or Calibration
steps.instructions: If the device provides an authorized user-accessible or service procedure for oxygen verification or calibration, perform it only according to the applicable manufacturer documentation and using approved test equipment. Do not invent calibration values or bypass failed calibration results. Expected outcome: Oxygen verification or calibration completes successfully and measured performance meets documented criteria.

steps.title: 9. Complete Functional Verification
steps.instructions: Verify stable airflow, oxygen delivery, relevant alarms, humidification, and overall operation across an appropriate controlled test condition. Expected outcome: Oxygen concentration is stable and within applicable criteria. Troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 10. Escalate Persistent Oxygen Errors
steps.instructions: If the oxygen source, tubing, settings, circuit, and external test equipment have been verified but concentration remains incorrect or calibration cannot be completed, stop external troubleshooting. Expected outcome: The Airvo 3 is removed from service for qualified oxygen-control or sensing evaluation.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported the measured oxygen concentration from the Airvo 3 was lower than expected.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the external oxygen supply tubing was partially kinked and restricting oxygen delivery.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering corrected the oxygen tubing routing, verified stable oxygen delivery with appropriate test equipment, and completed functional testing before return to service.

title: Fisher & Paykel Healthcare Airvo 3 High-Flow Oxygen System - Patient Circuit Leak Test Fails
description: Troubleshoots reported circuit leak or integrity failures caused by tubing, chamber, interface, connection, setup, or accessory problems.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Maintain Therapy
steps.instructions: Do not disconnect or manipulate a patient circuit while the patient depends on it. Transfer the patient to appropriate verified respiratory support before troubleshooting a suspected circuit leak. Expected outcome: Troubleshooting can proceed without interrupting required patient therapy.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Failure
steps.instructions: Determine whether staff observed an actual airflow leak, unstable therapy, a device message, inability to complete a setup check, or another symptom described as a "leak test failure." Record the displayed message and installed circuit components. Expected outcome: The exact failure is identified rather than assuming all low-flow conditions are caused by a leak.

steps.title: 3. Inspect the Breathing Tube and Patient Interface
steps.instructions: Examine the heated breathing tube, connectors, patient interface, adapters, and other externally accessible gas-path components for disconnection, cracks, tears, kinks, loose fittings, or improper assembly. Expected outcome: All respiratory components are intact and correctly connected. If reseating or replacing a defective external component restores normal operation, troubleshooting can stop after verification.

steps.title: 4. Inspect the Humidifier Chamber Installation
steps.instructions: Verify that the approved humidifier chamber is correctly installed and seated and that its connections are secure. Look for visible damage, incorrect assembly, or leakage. Do not alter chamber components or seals. Expected outcome: The chamber is correctly installed without visible leakage or damage.

steps.title: 5. Verify the Correct Circuit and Accessories
steps.instructions: Confirm that the breathing tube, interface, chamber, and adapters are compatible with the configured Airvo 3 setup and have not been mixed with incorrect or damaged accessories. Expected outcome: The device is configured with the intended compatible external components.

steps.title: 6. Check for Kinks, Obstructions, and Poor Positioning
steps.instructions: Inspect the full accessible tubing path. Correct sharp bends, compression, trapped tubing, excessive tension, or positioning that prevents secure connections. Expected outcome: The circuit remains open, properly routed, and securely connected.

steps.title: 7. Substitute Suspect External Components
steps.instructions: When appropriate, replace the suspect breathing tube, chamber, adapter, or interface with a known-good approved compatible component. Change one variable at a time. Expected outcome: A failed accessory is isolated if the condition disappears with the known-good component. Replace the defective accessory and continue to final verification.

steps.title: 8. Repeat the Applicable Functional Check
steps.instructions: With the patient disconnected and the circuit correctly assembled, repeat the normal setup or functional check specified for the device. Do not bypass alarms or force acceptance of a failed check. Expected outcome: The device completes the applicable circuit/setup verification and delivers stable flow.

steps.title: 9. Verify Functional Performance
steps.instructions: Confirm stable airflow, appropriate humidification operation, normal alarm function, and absence of unintended leaks before returning the unit to clinical use. Expected outcome: The Airvo 3 and complete external gas path function reliably. Troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 10. Escalate an Unresolved Failure
steps.instructions: If the condition persists with correctly assembled known-good compatible external components, stop external troubleshooting. A device-side sensing, flow-generation, connection, or control problem may require service evaluation. Expected outcome: The device is removed from clinical use for qualified evaluation.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported the Airvo 3 would not operate normally and appeared to have a leak in the patient circuit.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the heated breathing tube connection was not fully seated at the device.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering reseated the tubing, verified stable airflow and normal device operation, and completed functional testing before return to service.
